newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algeria's mobile voting booths hunt desert voters.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's mobile voting booths hunt desert voters.

text.p: Trucks equipped as mobile ballot stations set off before sunrise in Algeria's vast Sahara desert on Tuesday in pursuit of nomadic voters.
Algeria's weather service forecast daytime temperatures rising to around 40 degrees Celsius (104 Fahrenheit) as the trucks left, equipped with ballot boxes, food, water and communications.
The Sahara nomads, little affected by the violence that has shaken the north of the country, started voting on Monday, ahead of Thursday's general election, so that their results can be collated.
The official news agency APS said earlier that thousands were voting at six mobile "caravans" criss-crossing the 8,170 sq km Ghardaia region.
Other trucks were scouring isolated regions, and two caravans of 40 vehicles had left from Tindouf, deep in the desert south, at the weekend to serve distant localities.
International observers are accompanying the mobile polling stations.
